name: Ruching Palaung
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Shorto, H. L. 1960, 'Word and Syllable Patterns in Palaung', BSOAS 23(3):544-557 (paywalled; plausibly covers prominence in Palaung)

sources.citation: Buakaw, Rattanapitak & Deepadung. 2018. Katiang Palaung of Hsipaw: phonology and classification. Dialectologia 21: 1-16.
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: open copy online (also: harvard online access (harvardkey))
sources.note: Not pce (Katiang of Hsipaw, which the authors place between the Dehong group and the southern Darang dialects). p.5: 'The sesquisyllable consists of one main syllable preceded by a presyllable. Phonologically, presyllable is an unstressed syllable the vowel of which is limited to low central vowel /a/'; p.6: 'The minor syllable of Katiang is an unstressed syllable, namely a presyllable'. Same authors as the Dara'ang sketch.

sources.citation: Buakaw, Supakit. 2014. Vowel length in Da-ang dialect of Palaung spoken in Shan State, Myanmar. Dialectologia 12: 1-22.
sources.note: No prose statement on stress. Da-ang (Kalaw) is the Pale/Silver Palaung variety (pce). Phonetic transcriptions of sesquisyllabic words consistently place primary stress on the major (final) syllable: [saˈpən] 'lips', [saˈnaʔ] 'tender', [sɔˈdaːʔ] 'hot' (ex. 1, p.6); [kaˈtɛː] 'center', [kaˈpɔː] 'gourd', [ʔaˈsei] 'who', [maˈnou] 'teach' (ex. 2-3, p.7); uses the term 'major open syllables' (p.7).

sources.citation: Buakaw, Supakit. 2009. The phonetic realization of denasalized final nasal consonants in No Lae Palaung. Journal of Language and Culture (Mahidol) 28(1): 31-46.
sources.note: No statement on stress (paper is on final nasals of No Lae Dara-ang, Chiang Mai = pce). Incidental transcriptions mark stress on the final syllable: [ʔɨm ˈpac] 'saliva', [ˈkaːŋ] 'house' (p.33; legacy font renders ˈ as »).

sources.citation: Milne, Leslie. 1921. An Elementary Palaung Grammar. Oxford: Clarendon. / Shorto 1960 BSOAS 23(3) / Mak 2012 Golden Palaung.
sources.note: All describe Namhsan Ta-ang = Shwe Palaung (shwe1236), already in the catalog (Shorto 1960 p.556: major syllable carries more stress than the preceding minor syllable). Rosetta Project mislabels Milne 1921 as pce. Not this language; the earlier scan's named source Shorto 1960 is therefore the wrong languoid.

sources.citation: Lee, Wei-Wei. 2021. Verb-initial word order in Rucing Palaung: when nominal syntax goes clausal. PhD dissertation, University of Zurich (cumulative). DOI 10.5167/uzh-203130.
sources.note: Silent. Footnote 12, printed p.38 (PDF p.43): 'The phonology of Rucing is not yet fully understood and is not part of this study's purpose. Therefore, the broad phonemic transcriptions provided here should be taken as tentative.' Lists the phonological/lexical literature on Rucing as Janzen 1978; Shintani 2008; Buakaw 2009, 2012; Rattanapitak 2009 (p.37).

sources.citation: Deepadung, Sujaritlak & Supakit Buakaw. 2015. Raokot dialect of Palaung spoken in Yunnan: phonology and genetic classification. Journal of Language and Culture 34(2): 53-69.

sources.note: Consonants and vowels of Nor Lae (Dara-ang) Palaung only; no section on syllable structure, stress or suprasegmentals; IPA glyphs missing from the text layer.

sources.note: Comparative sound changes only; nothing on stress. Identifies Da-ang = Pale of Kalaw (Janzen 1991) and Dara-ang = No-Lae, both Darang group.
